name: Metal Nut Anomaly Detection
description: Dataset of metal nut images paired with a text prompt asking to detect the anomaly region, and binary segmentation masks localizing defects. It evaluates pixel-level anomaly segmentation for industrial inspection.
card_text: This dataset contains 37 samples from an industrial anomaly detection scenario focused on metal nuts. Each sample includes an RGB image of a metal nut, a fixed textual prompt instructing the model to detect the anomaly region, and a corresponding binary mask image that marks the anomalous area. The images are object-centric views of a single manufactured part, and the masks share the same base filename as the input image. The dataset is designed for evaluating segmentation-based anomaly localization, where the model must produce a spatial map of defects rather than a global label. The text prompt is short and instructional, while the visual content varies in anomaly appearance and location. The domain is manufacturing quality control.

question.semantics: A fixed instruction prompt asking the model to detect the anomaly region of the metal nut shown in the corresponding input image.

image.semantics: Path to an RGB image of a metal nut, which may contain surface or structural anomalies; serves as the visual input for localization.

mask.semantics: Path to a binary segmentation mask aligned with the input image, where anomalous regions of the metal nut are marked.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample has an input object containing an image_file that references a metal nut image and a prompt that instructs the model to detect the anomaly region, plus an output object containing a mask_file that references the corresponding binary segmentation mask. The image and prompt together specify the task, and the mask provides the pixel-level anomaly localization.
